title: Windsurf Operating Card
summary: Use the legacy Cascade workflow in Devin Desktop with explicit Ask/Code/Plan modes, durable workspace guidance, reviewed tool scope, named checkpoints, targeted recovery, and a runnable Node.js path-validation repair. Legacy Windsurf wording is retained in the title and slug for continuity. The overview uses Chat/Code terminology; current modes are Ask (search tools only), Code (edits and commands), and Plan (all tools enabled despite its planning purpose).
prerequisites: A Devin Desktop installation with access to the legacy Cascade workflow
An approved account and model policy, if required by the installation
Node.js 22 for the local learner exercise
A POSIX-compatible shell for the shown setup commands

sections.title: Choose Ask, Code, or Plan based on required authority
paragraphs: Product-name mapping: the official documentation retrieved on 2026-09-20 calls the product Devin Desktop and describes Cascade within it. This card retains the legacy Windsurf title and slug so existing links and curriculum references remain stable. It does not claim a rebrand date or history that the cited documentation does not establish. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade.

Do not treat every Devin experience as Cascade. The documentation distinguishes legacy Cascade from the default Devin Local agent experience. This card teaches the documented legacy Cascade workflow and does not transfer its controls or terminology to Devin Local. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories.

State the mode before work begins. Use Ask for explanation, inspection, and investigation that require search tools only and no edits or commands. Use Code only when the task authorizes edits or commands. Plan has all tools enabled despite its planning purpose, so planning intent alone is not a read-only guarantee. Separate product permission settings from the selected mode. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/modes.

The overview documentation uses the older Chat/Code terminology, while the modes documentation lists the current Ask/Code/Plan labels. In this card, Ask is the current label; Chat is mentioned only as the legacy overview term. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade and https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/modes.

Cascade supports plans, todo lists, tool calls, terminal awareness, and checkpoints. These capabilities do not remove the learner's responsibility to review the requested action, applicable task boundary, resulting diff, and verification output. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade.

The Node.js exercise in this card is a local correctness exercise. Passing it proves only that the supplied function satisfies the immutable test. It does not prove that Cascade selected a mode, followed durable guidance, created a checkpoint, or displayed any particular interface evidence.

sections.title: Make plans, rules, and checkpoints reviewable
paragraphs: Before implementation, fill a task card with one observable result, exact file scope, mode and tool boundaries, applicable durable guidance, a named checkpoint, verification evidence, and a recovery action. Treat the card as human-readable authorization for this task, not as an automatically enforced product permission configuration.

Start in Ask to inspect the request and propose a plan without edits or commands. Move to Code only for the authorized edit and local commands. Do not use Plan as a read-only mode because the modes documentation says it has all tools enabled. Network access is outside this task. If a proposed command, edit, tool call, or path falls outside the card, stop and revise the card rather than silently expanding scope.

Create a named Cascade checkpoint before risky work such as changing a path predicate. The cited documentation warns that a broad checkpoint revert is irreversible. Prefer inspected, targeted Git recovery when it can preserve unrelated work. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade.
The following worked example retains every task-card label and contains no placeholders.

In Devin Cascade Plan mode, the plan is written as external Markdown under `~/.devin/plans`; for a Windsurf agent, use the corresponding `~/.windsurf/plans` location. An `@mention` requests continuation, and Implement transitions to Code. Although the modes documentation says all tools are enabled, that is not a guarantee that Plan is read-only. These are workflow descriptions, not claims that this exercise has been executed. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/modes

code.label: Filled Cascade task card
code.code:
Task: Repair the path verifier so that it accepts only src/app and valid lexical descendants while rejecting sibling prefixes, malformed values, traversal segments, absolute paths, URLs, backslash-separated paths, and percent-encoded paths. Keep the immutable test unchanged.
Scope: Work only in a newly created cascade-path-repair directory. Edit starter.mjs only. Treat test.mjs, solution.mjs, and .devin/rules/path-repair.md as read-only after creation.
Permissions: Begin in Ask for inspection and plan review. Use Code only for the authorized one-predicate edit in starter.mjs and the listed local commands. Terminal scope is limited to node --version, node test.mjs ./starter.mjs, node test.mjs ./solution.mjs, git diff, git diff --stat, and git status --short. No network activity is authorized. These are task boundaries, not YAML permissions or a claim of automatic enforcement.
Rules: Read and apply .devin/rules/path-repair.md. Do not edit test.mjs. Change only the final authorization predicate in starter.mjs. Preserve the validation guards.
Checkpoint: pre-path-boundary-repair
Verification: Confirm Node.js reports major version 22. Run node test.mjs ./starter.mjs before editing and require the exact three-line failure shown in this card. Review the one-predicate diff. Run the same command after the learner repair and require PASS 15/15. Do not infer product behavior from local test output.
Recovery: Stop if scope expands. Inspect git diff and git status --short. Recover only the unintended hunk with a reviewed Git operation. Preserve unrelated edits, including pre-existing edits in the same file. Use the broad named checkpoint only after confirming that its irreversible revert will not discard work that must be retained.

sections.title: Reusable task-card template
paragraphs: Use this template for other Cascade tasks. Replace every bracketed field and review the completed card before entering Code.

code.label: Reusable Cascade task card
code.code:
Task: [one observable result]
Scope: [workspace and exact paths]
Permissions: [Ask, Code, or Plan boundary; terminal, edit, tools, and network limits]
Rules: [applicable .devin/rules file or AGENTS.md]
Checkpoint: [unique named recovery point created before risky work]
Verification: [plan review, requested-action review, diff, exact command, and exact expected result]
Recovery: [targeted recovery procedure, checkpoint limitation, and work that must be preserved]

sections.title: Store durable guidance in a documented location
paragraphs: The preferred location for durable Cascade guidance is `.devin/rules/*.md`, with `.windsurf/rules/*.md` as a fallback and the root `.windsurfrules` file as a legacy location. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories (verified 2026-09-20).

A root AGENTS.md is always active. An AGENTS.md in a nested directory is scoped to that directory. Rule frontmatter can use a glob trigger with globs patterns or the documented always_on, model_decision, and manual trigger forms. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories.

Memories can provide session context, but they are not a substitute for versioned project policy. Put team-reviewed durable guidance in a Rules file or AGENTS.md. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/memories.

The concrete rule below uses the documented preferred directory and glob-trigger frontmatter. Its Markdown body states reviewable guidance. It is not permission YAML, does not claim to disable product tools, and does not automatically enforce the task card's terminal, edit, or network boundaries.

code.label: .devin/rules/path-repair.md
code.code:
---
trigger: glob
globs: "*.mjs"
---

# Path repair boundary

- Treat `test.mjs` as immutable.
- For the learner repair, edit only the final authorization predicate in `starter.mjs`.
- Preserve the existing type and lexical-validation guards.
- Accept only `src/app` and descendants separated by the literal `/` character.
- Reject empty and non-string inputs, sibling prefixes, `.` or `..` segments, absolute paths, URLs, backslashes, and percent-encoded paths.
- Do not make network requests for this local task.
- Review the complete diff and exact test output before declaring the repair complete.
- Treat this text as durable guidance, not as an enforced permission configuration.

sections.title: Separate checkpoint recovery from targeted Git recovery
paragraphs: Create the named pre-path-boundary-repair checkpoint before changing the predicate. A broad checkpoint revert can be irreversible, so confirm exactly what it will replace before using it. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade.

For a small unintended change, first inspect the repository. `git restore --staged -p` can selectively unstage a hunk, while `git restore -p` can discard a selected working-tree hunk. The second operation destroys the selected uncommitted content, so review it before confirming.

Patch recovery can preserve unrelated changes in the same file when they appear in separable hunks. If intended and unintended edits overlap in one hunk, do not assume patch mode will separate them safely. Save or manually reconstruct the intended content before recovery.

code.label: Reviewed diff and targeted recovery commands
code.code:
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff -- starter.mjs solution.mjs test.mjs .devin/rules/path-repair.md

# If an unintended staged hunk exists, inspect and selectively unstage it:
git restore --staged -p -- path/to/file

# If an unintended working-tree hunk must be discarded, inspect each prompt carefully:
git restore -p -- path/to/file

# Inspect again after any recovery:
git status --short
git diff

sections.title: Define the lexical path policy before repairing the predicate
paragraphs: Allowed values are the root `src/app` and non-empty descendants such as `src/app/config.json` and `src/app/lib/index.js`.

The only recognized separator is the literal forward slash, `/`. Backslashes are rejected rather than normalized. Empty segments, including those produced by repeated or trailing separators, are rejected.

The policy rejects null, objects, all other non-string values, the empty string, `.` and `..` segments, absolute paths, URL-like strings with a scheme, and any value containing a percent sign. Rejecting every percent sign is a deliberately conservative encoded-path policy, so encoded separators and encoded traversal cannot be reinterpreted by a later decoder.

This is lexical validation. It does not access the filesystem, resolve symbolic links, establish file ownership, or create a filesystem sandbox. Code that later opens a path must separately address canonicalization, symlinks, race conditions, and operating-system access controls.

sections.title: Create a new workspace without deleting an existing directory
paragraphs: Run this setup once from a location where a new directory may be created. It generates a timestamp-and-process-based name and stops if that name already exists. It does not remove or overwrite an existing directory.

The local package manifest makes any CommonJS `.js` file placed in this fresh directory remain CommonJS even when the parent repository uses `type: module`. The exercise files below are `.mjs` and remain unchanged because `.mjs` is always treated as an ES module by Node.js.
After entering the new directory, create the four exercise artifacts and the rule file from the individually copyable sections below.

code.label: Fresh-directory setup
code.code:
set -eu
workspace="cascade-path-repair-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-$$"
if [ -e "$workspace" ]; then
  printf 'STOP: workspace already exists: %s\n' "$workspace" >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir "$workspace"
cd "$workspace"
printf '{"type":"commonjs"}\n' > package.json
printf 'Workspace: %s\n' "$PWD"
node --version

sections.title: Create the deliberately broken starter
paragraphs: Save this complete file as starter.mjs. Its validation guards are intact. The single defect is the final startsWith(ROOT) authorization predicate, which treats the sibling prefix src/application as though it were inside src/app.

Because the allowed root src/app also starts with ROOT, the starter passes both descendant controls and the root control. Its first failure in the immutable case order is therefore the changed sibling-prefix input.

code.label: starter.mjs

sections.title: Create the immutable test harness
paragraphs: Save this complete file as test.mjs and do not edit it during the learner repair. It uses node:assert/strict and dynamically imports the module path supplied as process.argv[2].

The first seven cases retain the established order: two allowed descendants, the allowed directory itself, the changed sibling-prefix input, an unrelated path, null, and a structurally invalid object. The remaining cases make the traversal, separator, absolute-path, URL, empty-value, and encoded-path policy executable.
The harness gathers failures and prints deterministic causal output instead of relying on environment-dependent stack paths.

code.label: test.mjs

sections.title: Create a tracked baseline before running the exercise
paragraphs: Use Bash, Git, and Node.js for this setup. Check Node with `node --version`; this card intends Node 22, although the supplied vendor sources do not independently confirm that exact version requirement.

Windsurf's offline setup creates fresh untracked files in the exercise directory. After every starter, test, solution, and rule file has been created, and while you are still in that fresh exercise directory, initialize Git there only. Do not run `git init` in a parent directory or in another repository.

The commands below track only this exercise's named baseline files. They do not add a remote, push anything, or remove or clean up files. The local identity is supplied on the commit command, so your global Git settings are unchanged. If a file name differs in the card, replace that name with the card's exact file name before running `git add`.

code.label: Initialize and commit the Windsurf exercise baseline
code.code:
node --version
git init
git add -- package.json .devin/rules/path-repair.md starter.mjs test.mjs solution.mjs
git -c user.name='Project 42 Learner' -c user.email='learner@example.invalid' commit -m 'Baseline exercise files'
# Confirm the baseline is clean before making learner changes.
git status --short
# Later, from this same exercise directory, inspect only tracked learner hunks:
git diff

sections.title: Run the starter, repair one predicate, and rerun it
paragraphs: First run the immutable test against starter.mjs. The exact expected standard-error lines are shown in the verification section. The process exits with status 1.

Then edit only the final authorization predicate in starter.mjs. Replace its character-prefix decision with a decision that accepts equality with ROOT or a prefix of ROOT followed by the literal separator. Do not edit the validation guards or test.mjs.
Run the same test command after the repair. The exact expected output is PASS 15/15. This learner workflow does not automatically execute the supplied solution.

code.label: Learner verification commands
code.code:
node test.mjs ./starter.mjs

# After observing the expected failure, edit only the final predicate in starter.mjs.
# Then rerun the same immutable test:
node test.mjs ./starter.mjs

# Review the learner's actual change:
git diff -- starter.mjs
git status --short

sections.title: Compare with the separate reviewed solution
paragraphs: Save this complete reference as solution.mjs, but do not copy it over starter.mjs as the learner repair. The validation code is identical to the starter. Only the final predicate changes.
After completing and reviewing the learner repair, the reference can be tested separately with node test.mjs ./solution.mjs. Its exact expected output is PASS 15/15.

code.label: solution.mjs

sections.title: Optionally test the reference after attempting the repair
paragraphs: This is a separate, explicit verification command. It is not part of setup and is not automatically executed for the learner.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: With the unmodified starter, the first three positive controls pass. The changed input src/application/config.json then fails because startsWith(ROOT) compares characters without requiring a directory boundary. The remaining validation cases pass, so the deterministic report contains exactly one failure.

The exact starter result is three standard-error lines: FAIL 1/15, sibling-prefix changed input: expected false, received true, and Cause: the authorization predicate crosses the src/app directory boundary. The process exits with status 1.
With the repaired starter or separate solution, the exact standard-output result is PASS 15/15 and the process exits with status 0.

The causal repair is the final predicate `value === ROOT || value.startsWith(`${ROOT}/`)`. Equality admits the allowed directory itself. Requiring ROOT followed by `/` admits genuine descendants while rejecting src/application. The earlier guards independently reject malformed inputs, traversal segments, unsupported separators, absolute paths, URLs, and percent-encoded paths.

Product-process evidence is separate from local correctness evidence. For a real Cascade run, inspect the selected Ask, Code, or Plan mode, the plan, requested tool actions, durable rule file, named checkpoint, full diff, commands, and output. The offline Node.js test makes no claim that this evidence exists or that any product control was automatically enforced.

code.label: Exact expected results
code.code:
Before the learner repair, stderr:
FAIL 1/15
sibling-prefix changed input: expected false, received true
Cause: the authorization predicate crosses the src/app directory boundary.

Before the learner repair, exit status:
1

After the learner repair, stdout:
PASS 15/15

After the learner repair, exit status:
0

Separate solution.mjs result:
PASS 15/15
